tools.security_considerations: The -exec action executes arbitrary commands with the privileges of the invoking user. When find possesses the SetUID bit, -exec spawns processes with elevated effective user IDs, enabling privilege escalation via GTFOBins.

tools.description: grep searches for PATTERNS in each FILE. PATTERNS is one or more patterns separated by newline characters, and grep prints each line that matches a pattern.
tools.security_considerations: Grepping recursively across /proc or /sys can hang on infinite virtual file streams. Use --exclude-dir and -I to skip binary or device files.

tools.description: Gawk is the GNU Project's implementation of the AWK programming language. It is a powerful pattern scanning and text processing language commonly used for columnar data parsing and protocol dissection.
tools.security_considerations: Awk can execute system commands using the system() function or pipes, which can lead to command injection if input parameters are not sanitized.

tools.description: Sed is a stream editor used to perform basic text transformations on an input stream (a file or input from a pipeline).
tools.security_considerations: The 'e' flag in substitution commands executes the replacement text in a shell. In SUID contexts or scripts, this can lead to arbitrary code execution.

tools.description: ExifTool is a platform-independent Perl library plus a command-line application for reading, writing and manipulating metadata in a wide variety of files.
tools.security_considerations: Past vulnerabilities (e.g. CVE-2021-22204) in DjVu and other parser modules allowed unauthenticated remote code execution via malformed metadata chunks.

tools.description: Binwalk is a fast, easy to use tool for analyzing, reverse engineering, and extracting firmware images and arbitrary binary streams.
tools.security_considerations: Unpacking untrusted firmware archives with -e can expose path traversal vulnerabilities or trigger malicious symlinks. Always extract inside an isolated unprivileged directory.

tools.description: Steghide is a steganography program that is able to hide data in various kinds of image and audio files (BMP, JPEG, WAV, AU).
tools.security_considerations: Steghide uses graph theory and Rijndael encryption. Brute-forcing passwords against steghide files requires tools like stegcracker.

tools.description: TShark is a network protocol analyzer. It lets you capture packet data from a live network, or read packets from a previously saved capture file.
tools.security_considerations: Complex protocol dissectors parsing malformed network frames may trigger memory corruption bugs. Run tshark under unprivileged service accounts without root permissions.

tools.description: The OpenSSL command line tool provides rich cryptographic functionality including cipher suites, public key generation, X.509 certificate management, and PRNG testing.
tools.security_considerations: Weak key generation (e.g. RSA keys < 2048 bits or deterministic entropy sources) severely degrades asymmetric cryptosystem security.

tools.description: curl is a tool for transferring data from or to a server using one of the supported protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, etc.).
tools.security_considerations: curl sends credentials in cleartext over unencrypted HTTP. Use --tlsv1.2 or higher for secure communications.

tools.description: socat is a relay for bidirectional data transfer between two independent data channels. Each channel can be a file, pipe, device, socket, or process.
tools.security_considerations: socat can be used to spawn encrypted or unencrypted reverse shells (e.g. TCP-LISTEN:port,exec:/bin/bash).

tools.description: The purpose of a debugger such as GDB is to allow you to see what is going on `inside' another program while it executes -- or what another program was doing at the moment it crashed.
tools.security_considerations: GDB attaches to processes via the ptrace system call. ptrace allows arbitrary memory read and write, register modification, and execution redirection.
